title: How to Store Fresh Herbs So They Last Longer

seo.title: How to Store Fresh Herbs So They Last Longer
seo.meta_description: Fresh herbs last longer when moisture and dehydration are managed according to their texture.
seo.search_intent: Use a practical, safe method to store Fresh Herbs So They Last Longer, with clear checks, limits, and next steps.

excerpt: Fresh herbs last longer when moisture and dehydration are managed according to their texture. Tender herbs such as cilantro or parsley often do well like cut flowers, while sturdy herbs such as rosemary and thyme generally prefer a drier setup.
content_html:
Fresh herbs last longer when moisture and dehydration are managed according to their texture. Tender herbs such as cilantro or parsley often do well like cut flowers, while sturdy herbs such as rosemary and thyme generally prefer a drier setup.

Remove damaged leaves and stems before storage

Crushed or slimy leaves accelerate spoilage and keep healthy leaves wet. Remove damaged pieces and avoid packing a bunch tightly when parts are already deteriorating.

Treat tender herbs like a small bouquet

Trim the stem ends of parsley, cilantro, or mint and stand them in a small amount of water without submerging the leaves. In the refrigerator, a loose bag can reduce dehydration without trapping excessive condensation.

Keep sturdy herbs somewhat drier

Rosemary, thyme, and sage often store well loosely wrapped in barely damp paper inside a container or bag. The goal is to prevent wilting without leaving the leaves wet.

Check smell, texture, and visible mold before use

Discard slimy leaves, visible mold, or herbs with a clearly altered odor. Whether you wash before storage or just before use depends on the herb and method, but washed leaves should be dried well so they are not stored wet.
